text.title: PWA Advanced Features Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules on Web Push (VAPID key handling, subscription lifecycle, permission timing), offline mutation queues over IndexedDB + Background Sync, and the platform preconditions that make the whole feature set unavailable. Checkable against the subscribe call, the push-send worker and the sync handler.

rule.statement: One P-256 VAPID key pair per application. The public key is passed to `pushManager.subscribe({ userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey })` as the raw 65-byte uncompressed point (base64url); the private key exists only server-side and MUST NOT be rotated without a re-subscribe migration.

rationale.source: RFC 8292 (Voluntary Application Server Identification for Web Push)

rule.rationale: The push service records the application server key at subscribe time and validates the JWT on every send against it. Rotating the key does not invalidate anything client-side — existing subscriptions simply start returning 403 on send, so delivery drops to zero while the client still believes it is subscribed.

rule.statement: The `push` handler MUST call `self.registration.showNotification()` inside `event.waitUntil()` on every delivery. Silent data-only pushes are forbidden on the web path.
rule.rationale: `subscribe()` without `userVisibleOnly: true` rejects with NotSupportedError in Chromium. When a handler resolves without showing a notification, the browser substitutes a generic "This site has been updated in the background" notification; repeated occurrences are treated as budget abuse and the origin's push permission is revoked without user action.

rule.statement: `Notification.requestPermission()` MUST be called from a user gesture handler attached to an explicit opt-in control that states what will be sent. Calling it on page load, on first route render, or inside an effect is rejected.

rationale.source: Chromium quiet notification UI / abusive-permission-request policy

rule.rationale: Permission state is per-origin and `denied` cannot be recovered from JavaScript — only through browser settings, which users never open. Origins with a low prompt-acceptance rate are additionally enrolled in quiet UI, where the prompt is suppressed for all future visitors, so one page-load prompt permanently caps the channel.

rule.statement: The send worker MUST delete the stored subscription row on HTTP 404 or 410 from the push endpoint, honour `Retry-After` on 429, and record `last_success_at` per subscription.

rationale.source: RFC 8030 (Generic Event Delivery Using HTTP Push)

rule.rationale: 410 Gone means the subscription is permanently invalid — the user cleared site data, uninstalled, or the browser rotated the endpoint. Retrying it forever inflates the queue with guaranteed failures and, because those failures are counted as sends, the reported delivery rate stays plausible while real reach collapses.

rule.statement: Every mutation written to the IndexedDB outbox MUST carry a client-generated idempotency key (UUIDv4) sent as a header or body field, and the server MUST dedupe on it for at least the retry window.
rule.rationale: A `sync` event fires again with backoff whenever the handler's `waitUntil` promise rejects, and it also fires again if the browser terminates the worker before the promise settles. A request that already reached the server but failed to return before termination is therefore replayed, so a non-idempotent POST creates duplicate records that look like user error.

rule.statement: Background Sync MUST use a single stable tag (e.g. `outbox-flush`) whose handler drains every pending IndexedDB record in order. Per-item tags (`sync-<recordId>`) are rejected.

rationale.source: Background Synchronization API — tag uniqueness + registration limits

rule.rationale: Registrations are keyed by tag, so re-registering a pending tag coalesces — which is the desired behaviour. Per-item tags instead create an unbounded set of registrations that the browser throttles and drops under its retry budget, and dropped registrations produce no event and no error, so the affected records sit in IndexedDB forever.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) iOS Safari is the primary platform and the requirement includes Background Sync or Periodic Background Sync — neither is implemented in WebKit; (b) Web Push is required on iOS below 16.4, or for users who will not add the app to the Home Screen, since iOS delivers Web Push only to home-screen-installed web apps; (c) a native shell (Capacitor, Tauri, React Native) is already present — use APNs/FCM through the shell instead of a second push channel.
rule.rationale: Two parallel push channels on the same device double-deliver, because the web subscription and the native token are independent and neither knows about the other; the user sees every notification twice and disables both.
